Lesson · 25 min

Message Your Team in Google Chat

Use Google Chat for quick team conversations: direct messages, spaces, @mentions, reactions, and sharing Drive files with the right access.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Open Google Chat in Gmail and start a direct message or a group message
  • ✓Create a space and add people to it
  • ✓Mention someone with @, and decide whether to add them to the space
  • ✓Share a Google Drive file in a message and choose the access people get
  • ✓Decide when a message belongs in Chat and when it belongs in email

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Quick questions, without the email thread

On the job

You're coordinating the Riverside Commons lobby repaint.

The repaint starts next week. Kim needs to check the lobby lights, Andre needs to know prospects should use the side door, and everyone needs the repaint schedule. Ten short emails would bury the office. Parkview uses Google Chat for quick team conversations like these.

Your task: Send a direct message, post updates in the team space, share the schedule, and set up a new space.

Google Chat is Google's messaging app. You can use it at chat.google.com or inside Gmail: select Chat on the far left of Gmail. Chat has direct messages (DMs) between two or more people, and spaces, where a team or project keeps its conversation, files, and members in one place.

Key terms

Direct message (DM)
A private conversation with one person, or a group DM with a few people.
Space
A named place for a team or project conversation. People can be added or leave, and new members see the conversation.
@mention
Typing @ and a name in a message so that person gets a notification.
Reaction
An emoji you add to a message to answer without writing a new one.
Shortcuts
Home, Mentions, and Starred at the top of Chat's left side. Mentions lists messages where someone mentioned you.
Microsoft Teams users: Google Chat's direct messages are like Teams chats, and spaces are like channels in a team.

Direct messages

  1. In Gmail, select Chat on the far left (or open chat.google.com).
  2. Select New chat at the top left.
  3. Enter a name or email address. For a group message, add more names.
  4. Select Start chat, type your message in the box at the bottom, and select Send (or press Enter).
💡 The first time you message someone, they may need to accept your message request before you can chat. If your work account allows chatting with people outside your organization, their names show an External badge, so you always know when a conversation includes outsiders.

Spaces for teams and projects

  1. Select New chat › Create a space.
  2. Enter a space name. You can also choose an emoji for the space's picture.
  3. Select Create.
  4. In the space, select Add people, pick the people, and select Add.

A space keeps a project together: the conversation, the files people share, and the list of members. When the lobby repaint is over, the space still holds the whole history. With a personal Google Account you can create spaces for collaborating with others; work accounts may have more kinds of spaces, depending on your organization.

Mentions, reactions, and files

Worked example

Sharing the repaint schedule

Get the schedule to everyone in the Riverside Commons Team space.

  1. 1

    Type “Here's the repaint schedule.” then @Lobby, and pick Lobby Repaint Schedule under Files.

    The message carries a link to the one current file, not a copy.

  2. 2

    Press Enter. Chat says some members can't open the file and asks for the type of access.

    Sharing in Chat also shares the file in Drive.

  3. 3

    Choose Viewer and select Send.

    The team needs to read the schedule, not change it. Give the least access that does the job.

Result: Everyone in the space can open the schedule, and it stays up to date when Denise changes it.

🔑 Share the Drive file, not a downloaded copy, and pick the access level on purpose.

Chat is still work communication. Don't post tenants' private information, such as bank details or Social Security numbers, in a space, and remember that people added later can read the space's history.

Knowledge Check

Check your understanding

You @mention Andre in a space he isn't in yet, and you want him to see the conversation. Which option do you choose?

Check your understanding

Where should a project's ongoing team conversation go?

Coordinate the lobby repaint in Google Chat

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Practice with a classmate or a second Google Account of your own. Personal Google Accounts can use Google Chat at chat.google.com or in Gmail.

  1. Start a direct message with your partner and send a short hello.
  2. Create a space named “Study Group” and add your partner.
  3. In the space, @mention your partner with a question, and add a reaction to their answer.
  4. Share a Google Doc from your Drive in the space, giving your partner Commenter access.
  5. Write two sentences: one message you'd send in Chat and one you'd send by email, and why.
Deliverable: Submit a screenshot of your space showing the mention, the reaction, and the shared file, plus your two sentences, to your instructor or course folder. If you can't use Google Chat, complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
